subject: Physics
title: Electrostatics
summary: Charge has three properties: it is quantised (q = ne), conserved (never created or destroyed) and additive (add with sign). The force between two charges follows Coulomb's law — inverse square, along the line joining them.

Electric field E = force per unit positive test charge. For several charges add their fields as vectors (superposition). For a continuous distribution (rod, ring, sheet) take small pieces dq and integrate.
Gauss's law: total flux out of a closed surface = enclosed charge / ε₀. Where there is symmetry (line, sheet, sphere) it is the fastest way to find the field.
Potential V is a scalar (just add, no direction) and E = −dV/dr. The field always points towards decreasing potential. Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to field lines.
Inside a conductor the electrostatic field is zero, all excess charge sits on the surface, and the whole conductor is at one potential.

A capacitor stores charge and energy: C = Q/V. Parallel plate C = Kε₀A/d. In series Q is the same, in parallel V is the same — exactly opposite to resistors. What changes when a dielectric is inserted depends on whether the battery is still connected.

formulas.name: Coulomb's law
formulas.formula: F = k q₁q₂ / r²,   k = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²,   ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²)
formulas.when: Force between two point charges (vacuum/air).
formulas.note: Use signs only to decide direction; use |q| for the magnitude.

formulas.name: Coulomb's law in a medium
formulas.formula: F_medium = F_vacuum / K   (K = dielectric constant = ε/ε₀)
formulas.when: Charges placed in a medium (water, oil).
formulas.note: K ≥ 1 always, so the force is smaller in a medium.

formulas.name: Quantisation and conservation
formulas.formula: q = n e,   e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C,   n integer
formulas.when: How many electrons moved; charge is always an integer multiple of e.

formulas.name: Superposition
formulas.formula: F_net = F₁ + F₂ + …   (vector sum),   E_net = Σ Eᵢ
formulas.when: Three or more charges; find each pair's force, then add as vectors.

formulas.name: Field of a point charge
formulas.formula: E = F/q₀ = k q / r²   (away from q if q is positive)
formulas.when: Field at a point.

formulas.name: Continuous charge distribution
formulas.formula: dq = λ dl,  σ dA,  ρ dV;    E = ∫ k dq / r²  (keeping track of direction)
formulas.when: Rods, rings, discs with spread-out charge.
formulas.note: First remove components that cancel by symmetry.

formulas.name: Ring of charge on its axis
formulas.formula: E = k Q x / (x² + R²)^{3/2};   at the centre E = 0;   E_max at x = R/√2
formulas.when: Field at a point on the axis of a ring.

formulas.name: Electric dipole moment
formulas.formula: p = q × (2a),   direction from −q to +q
formulas.when: Two equal and opposite charges separated by 2a.

formulas.name: Dipole field (r ≫ a)
formulas.formula: Axial: E = 2kp/r³ (along p).   Equatorial: E = kp/r³ (opposite to p).   General: E = (kp/r³)√(1 + 3cos²θ)
formulas.when: Field far from a dipole.
formulas.note: A dipole field falls as 1/r³, a point charge's as 1/r².

formulas.name: Dipole in uniform field
formulas.formula: τ = p × E,  |τ| = pE sin θ;   net force F = 0
formulas.when: In a uniform field a dipole only rotates.
formulas.note: In a non-uniform field there is also a net force.

formulas.name: Dipole potential energy
formulas.formula: U = −p·E = −pE cos θ;   W(θ₁→θ₂) = pE (cos θ₁ − cos θ₂)
formulas.when: Work to rotate a dipole, stable/unstable positions.
formulas.note: θ = 0 stable (U = −pE), θ = 180° unstable (U = +pE). Work from 0 to 180° = 2pE.

formulas.name: Electric flux
formulas.formula: Φ = ∮ E·dA = E A cos θ  (uniform field, flat surface)
formulas.when: How many field lines cross a surface.
formulas.note: θ is the angle between the field and the area vector (normal).

formulas.name: Gauss's law
formulas.formula: Φ_closed = q_enclosed / ε₀
formulas.when: Closed surface; flux depends only on charge inside.
formulas.mistake: Outside charges don't change the total flux, but they do change E on the surface.

formulas.name: Infinite line charge
formulas.formula: E = λ / (2πε₀ r) = 2kλ / r
formulas.when: Long straight wire (Gauss: cylinder).

formulas.name: Infinite plane sheet
formulas.formula: E = σ / (2ε₀)  (independent of r).   Between two oppositely charged plates: E = σ/ε₀, outside 0
formulas.when: Field near a large flat sheet.
formulas.mistake: Just outside a conductor's surface E = σ/ε₀, not σ/2ε₀.

formulas.name: Thin spherical shell (charge Q)
formulas.formula: r > R: E = kQ/r²,  V = kQ/r.   r = R: E = kQ/R².   r < R: E = 0,  V = kQ/R (constant)
formulas.when: Shell or conducting sphere.
formulas.note: Inside, E is zero but V is not.

formulas.name: Uniformly charged solid sphere (non-conducting)
formulas.formula: r < R: E = kQr/R³ (grows with r);   r ≥ R: E = kQ/r²
formulas.when: Insulating solid sphere — common Gauss's-law practice in JEE.

formulas.name: Potential and field
formulas.formula: V = kq/r;   V_A − V_B = −∫_B^A E·dr;   E = −dV/dr  (E_x = −∂V/∂x)
formulas.when: Potential from field or field from potential.
formulas.note: V is a scalar: add potentials of many charges directly (with sign).

formulas.name: Dipole potential
formulas.formula: V = k p cos θ / r²;   V = 0 on the equatorial line
formulas.when: Potential far from a dipole.
formulas.mistake: On the equatorial line V = 0 but E is not zero.

formulas.name: Potential energy of charges
formulas.formula: Two charges: U = k q₁q₂ / r.   System: U = Σ (each pair) k qᵢqⱼ / rᵢⱼ
formulas.when: Work to assemble a system.
formulas.note: Count each pair only once (3 charges = 3 pairs).

formulas.name: Work and energy in a field
formulas.formula: W_ext = q ΔV;   charge accelerated through V volt: K = qV  (1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J)
formulas.when: Moving or accelerating a charge.
formulas.note: Work along an equipotential is zero.

formulas.name: Capacitance
formulas.formula: C = Q/V.   Parallel plate: C = ε₀A/d.   Isolated sphere: C = 4πε₀R
formulas.when: Capacity of a capacitor.

formulas.name: Capacitor with dielectric
formulas.formula: Completely filled: C = Kε₀A/d.   Slab of thickness t: C = ε₀A / (d − t + t/K).   Metal slab: C = ε₀A / (d − t)
formulas.when: Dielectric or metal between the plates.
formulas.note: A metal slab is the K → ∞ case.

formulas.name: Combination of capacitors
formulas.formula: Series: 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + …  (same Q on each).   Parallel: C = C₁ + C₂ + …  (same V on each)
formulas.when: Capacitor networks.
formulas.note: Opposite of resistors: the series equivalent is smaller than the smallest capacitor.

formulas.name: Energy stored
formulas.formula: U = ½CV² = Q²/(2C) = ½QV;   energy density u = ½ ε₀ E²  (in a medium ½ε₀KE²)
formulas.when: Energy of a capacitor.

formulas.name: Dielectric inserted — battery ON vs OFF
formulas.formula: Battery ON: V same, C→KC, Q→KQ, U→KU.   Battery OFF: Q same, C→KC, V→V/K, E→E/K, U→U/K
formulas.when: What changes after inserting a dielectric.

formulas.name: Charge sharing between capacitors
formulas.formula: Common V = (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂)/(C₁ + C₂);   heat loss = C₁C₂(V₁ − V₂)² / [2(C₁ + C₂)]
formulas.when: Connecting a charged capacitor to another.
formulas.note: Energy always decreases (heat/radiation); charge is conserved.

formulas.name: Induced charge on dielectric and plate force
formulas.formula: Q_induced = Q(1 − 1/K);   attraction between plates F = Q²/(2ε₀A)
formulas.when: Charge on dielectric surfaces; pull between plates.
formulas.note: The ½ appears because a plate feels no force from its own field.

examples.title: Force between two charges
examples.problem: q₁ = +2 μC and q₂ = −3 μC are 30 cm apart in air. Size and nature of the force?
examples.solution: F = kq₁q₂/r² = 9 × 10⁹ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 3 × 10⁻⁶ / (0.3)² = 0.6 N. The charges are opposite, so it is attractive.

examples.title: Where is the field zero?
examples.problem: +4q is at x = 0 and +q at x = 30 cm. Where between them is E = 0?
examples.solution: For like charges the null point lies between them, nearer the smaller charge. At distance x from 4q: k(4q)/x² = kq/(30 − x)² ⇒ x/(30 − x) = 2 ⇒ x = 20 cm (10 cm from q). For unlike charges the null point lies outside, on the side of the smaller charge.

examples.title: Torque and work on a dipole
examples.problem: ±2 μC charges are 2 cm apart; the dipole makes 30° with E = 5 × 10⁵ N/C. Torque? Work to rotate it from 0° to 180°?

examples.title: Charge at the centre of a cube
examples.problem: q = 1.77 μC sits at the centre of a cube. Flux through the whole cube and through one face?
examples.solution: Total Φ = q/ε₀ = 1.77 × 10⁻⁶ / 8.85 × 10⁻¹² ≈ 2.0 × 10⁵ N·m²/C. By symmetry the 6 faces share it equally: one face = q/(6ε₀) ≈ 3.3 × 10⁴ N·m²/C. (If the charge is at a corner, flux through the whole cube is q/(8ε₀); the 3 faces touching that corner get zero flux because the field is parallel to them.)

examples.title: Shell: E zero inside, V not
examples.problem: A thin shell of R = 10 cm carries Q = 1 nC. E and V at the centre? V at 20 cm?
examples.solution: Inside E = 0. Inside V = surface value = kQ/R = 9 × 10⁹ × 10⁻⁹ / 0.1 = 90 V. At r = 0.2 m, V = kQ/r = 45 V.

examples.title: Capacitor network
examples.problem: 3 μF and 6 μF in series; this pair is in parallel with 4 μF; connected to 12 V. C_eq, total charge, energy?
examples.solution: Series: 3×6/(3+6) = 2 μF. Parallel: 2 + 4 = 6 μF. Q = CV = 6 × 12 = 72 μC. U = ½CV² = ½ × 6 × 10⁻⁶ × 144 = 432 μJ.

examples.title: Dielectric after removing the battery
examples.problem: A 10 pF capacitor is charged to 100 V and the battery is removed. A K = 5 dielectric then fills the gap. New V and energy?
examples.solution: Battery OFF ⇒ Q stays = CV = 1 nC. C → 50 pF, V → 100/5 = 20 V. U before = ½CV² = 50 nJ, after = U/K = 10 nJ. Energy decreases — the slab is pulled in (the external agent does negative work).

examples.title: Energy lost in charge sharing
examples.problem: A 2 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is connected to an uncharged 3 μF capacitor. Common V and heat loss?
examples.solution: V = C₁V₁/(C₁ + C₂) = 200/5 = 40 V. Before: U = ½ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 100² = 10 mJ; after: ½ × 5 × 10⁻⁶ × 40² = 4 mJ. Loss = 6 mJ — the formula C₁C₂ΔV²/[2(C₁+C₂)] = 6 × 10⁻¹² × 10⁴ / 10⁻⁵ gives the same.

examples.title: Electron accelerated through 100 V
examples.problem: An electron starts from rest and passes through a potential difference of 100 V. KE and speed?

topics.title: Charge and charging by induction
topics.explain: Charge is quantised, conserved and additive. In induction, bring a charged rod near, earth the far side, remove the earth, then the rod — the conductor keeps an opposite charge. The rod loses none of its own charge.

topics.title: Rules of electric field lines
topics.explain: They start on positive and end on negative charges. They never cross (a point can't have two field directions). Crowded lines = strong field. They don't form closed loops in electrostatics. They meet conductor surfaces at right angles.

topics.title: Dipole: uniform vs non-uniform field
topics.explain: In a uniform field the forces on the two charges are equal and opposite ⇒ net force 0, only torque (it rotates and aligns). In a non-uniform field there is also a net force — the dipole is pulled towards the stronger field (like bits of paper towards a charged comb).

topics.title: When and how to use Gauss's law
topics.explain: Useful only with symmetry: line charge → coaxial cylinder, sheet → pillbox, sphere → concentric sphere. Choose a Gaussian surface where E is constant and perpendicular (or parallel) to the surface. Flux depends only on the charge inside; the field depends on all charges.

topics.title: Conductors in electrostatics
topics.explain: Inside E = 0; excess charge lies only on the outer surface; at the surface E is perpendicular with magnitude σ/ε₀; the whole conductor is equipotential. σ is larger at sharp points (hence pointed lightning conductors). Inside a hollow conductor (with no charge in the cavity) the field is zero — electrostatic shielding. An insulator, by contrast, does not let charge move freely.

topics.title: Potential, potential difference and energy
topics.explain: V = work per unit charge to bring it from infinity. ΔV between two points is independent of path (conservative field). A positive charge moves from high V to low V; an electron the opposite way. The field is the slope of potential (−dV/dr).

topics.title: Equipotential surfaces
topics.explain: Surfaces on which V is the same everywhere. Field lines are perpendicular to them. No work is done moving a charge along them. Point charge: concentric spheres; uniform field: parallel planes perpendicular to the field. Two equipotentials never intersect.

topics.title: Dielectrics and polarisation
topics.explain: A dielectric is an insulator that gets polarised in a field. Polar molecules (H₂O) have permanent dipoles that align; non-polar ones (O₂) get induced dipoles. The field inside drops to E₀/K, so capacitance becomes K times.

topics.title: How a capacitor works
topics.explain: Two conductors carry +Q and −Q. C depends only on geometry and medium, not on Q or V. Energy is stored in the field between the plates (u = ½ε₀E²).

topics.title: Logic of series vs parallel
topics.explain: In series every capacitor has the same Q (induced on the inner plates) and V divides — the smaller C gets the larger V. In parallel V is the same and Q divides — the larger C gets more Q.

topics.title: Dielectric: battery connected or not
topics.explain: Connected (V fixed): C, Q, U all become K times. Disconnected (Q fixed): V, E, U all become 1/K. If asked 'where did the energy go' — with the battery ON it did extra work; with it OFF the energy decreased and the slab was pulled in.

ratta: Field: point 1/r², dipole 1/r³, line 1/r, sheet independent of r.
Shell: inside E = 0, V = kQ/R (constant).  Solid sphere inside E ∝ r.
Dipole: τ = pE sin θ,  U = −pE cos θ,  work 0 → 180° = 2pE.
Cube centre: one face q/6ε₀;  charge at a corner: whole cube q/8ε₀.
Capacitors: series → add 1/C (same Q);  parallel → add C (same V).
Battery ON: V same → Q, U become K times.  Battery OFF: Q same → V, U become 1/K.
Ring axis: E_max at x = R/√2.
Conductor: E = 0 inside, E = σ/ε₀ at surface (perpendicular), whole body equipotential.
